pages.text: Two rails and an armature between them: current up one rail, across, down the other. The field between the rails pushes the armature out with $(thing)F = ½L′I²$() - a railgun.

Set the current and the armature's mass. It leaves at $(thing)v = √(2FL/m)$() and strikes the target with a shock of about $(thing)½ρv²$(). Graphite shocked between 15 and 40 GPa becomes $(item)Lonsdaleite$(), hexagonal diamond, as in meteorite craters; sand and coal at 50-90 GPa fuse into moissanite. Each shot spends a Rail Armature. Above 3 MA the rails erode.
